why:
non-blocking read of the `CancelReturnCode` for a cancel this client sent. rclcpp_action has no counterpart because its cancel is a future; ours is the read half of the fire-then-read pair described at `cpp:Client::cancel_goal`. `nros::CancelReturnCode` (the RPC outcome) is deliberately a different type from `nros::CancelResponse` (the per-goal decision) -- `check-cpp` instantiates a TU that static-asserts they stay distinct.

phase-428 (RFC-0089): re-keyed by the namespace flip. `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` are now aliases of `rclcpp_action::Client<A>` / `rclcpp_action::Server<A>`, which the extractor keys as `Client::*` / `Server::*`. The type is `same` now and the member is `ours-only`, so it no longer inherits its type's verdict and carries its own.

issue 2034 (2026-10-25) -- the executor's spin now TAKES cancel replies (freeing each request's slot) and hands them to the C++ client; a reply no `async_cancel_*` future or callback claims is kept, oldest first, for this read (`rclcpp_action::CANCEL_STASH_CAP` = 4 per client; a further unread reply evicts the oldest). A reply nothing has taken yet is still read straight off the client. Held by `action_cancel_reply_spin_runtime.cpp`.
